app.title: HyetiaScan 2.1.2
app.summary: A person uploads a CSV of rain-gauge readings, checks the column types and a preview of the records, and picks which column holds the date-time and which holds the precipitation. The readings are aligned to the estimated logging interval. The person then deals with each kind of abnormal reading (duplicate, corrupt, outlier above a threshold, missing), while charts and a pie show how many of each remain per day, month or year. Events are only computed once no abnormal readings are left. The person then sets the event criteria (date range, minimum and maximum duration, minimum intensity, maximum pause) and reads the resulting events through summary statistics, Huff curves by quartile, frequency curves, intensity-range counts and rainfall accumulated over fixed time spans.

task.text: Clean a precipitation time series of abnormal readings, then split it into rain events and characterise them by duration, intensity, Huff quartile and accumulated depth.

data.text: A CSV time series of precipitation depth per reading at a regular logging interval, cleaned and then grouped into discrete rain events, each with derived attributes.
data.item: a precipitation reading at one timestamp, and later a rain event made of contiguous readings

stage.text: cleaning raw rain-gauge logs and extracting storm events, before design or hydrological modelling

mechanism.text: Tabs move through the stages in order: preview the file, clean the readings, then events. The cleaning controls rerun the grouped quality counts and charts every time they change, and the Events tab stays blocked until no abnormal readings are left. A parameter column beside the Events tab recomputes the events, and sub-tabs show statistics, Huff curves, frequency curves, intensity ranges and accumulations for that event set.

field.text: rainfall event separation and Huff-curve analysis in hydrology

workflow.name: clean a logged time series, then segment it into events and characterise them

steps.here: Upload a CSV in the sidebar, with the decimal separator and encoding set in a config tab. Then choose the date-time and precipitation columns from the columns of the right type. The logging interval is estimated and the timestamps are aligned to it.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The Archivo tab lists each column with its detected type, flags the first date-time format error, and previews as many rows as a slider sets.

Radio choices handle duplicates (keep first or last, sum, average, delete), delete corrupt (negative) readings, delete outliers above an editable threshold, and fill missing intervals with zero. The counts per category then recompute.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Accumulated precipitation and abnormal-reading counts are charted by day, month or year, and a pie gives each category's count and percentage. Events stay blocked until every abnormal count is zero.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Set a date range, minimum and maximum duration, minimum intensity, maximum pause, and whether a pause equal to the maximum still counts as rain. Contiguous readings become events with duration, intensity, depth and a Huff quartile.

Sub-tabs show descriptive statistics and an event table with chosen columns, average Huff curves per quartile at a chosen percentile step, frequency curves of duration and depth with interpolated tables, event counts by intensity range and quartile, and depth accumulated over fixed spans of 10–120 minutes.

distinctive: Abnormal readings fall into four named kinds (missing, duplicate, corrupt, outlier), each with its own fix. Event analysis is locked until none remain.
Events are defined by a continuity rule: zero readings shorter than a maximum pause join the rain on either side. A switch decides whether a pause exactly equal to the maximum joins or separates.
Each event gets a Huff quartile: the quarter of its duration in which most of its rain fell. Curves are averaged per quartile.
Timestamps are aligned to a logging interval taken as the mode of the gaps between the first readings.
